title: Savings pots and round-ups automation
summary: Two hypothesis-led setups for enabling weekly recurring saving and card round-ups on an existing savings pot, drawn from the savings example PRD.

brief.primaryUser: A retail current-account customer who already uses savings pots
brief.job: Put money aside steadily for a future life event without turning saving into another chore
brief.journey: Open an existing pot, enable weekly recurring saving and card round-ups, review the money movement, and confirm
brief.decision: Whether compact direct controls or a guided explanation better balance setup speed and trust

variants.label: Focused control
variants.hypothesis: Experienced pot users set up automation faster when every control is visible on one compact screen with immediate review
tradeOffs: Less progressive explanation before money moves
Round-up rules must be sought via the details control

variants.label: Guided trust
variants.hypothesis: Sequencing cadence, amount, and round-up explanations before confirmation improves trust in automated money movement
tradeOffs: More steps and navigation to reach a confirmed state
Experienced users may feel slowed down

scenarios.label: Happy path
scenarios.description: Choose weekly saving, enter £25, enable round-ups, review, confirm, and observe Automation is set

scenarios.label: Validation error
scenarios.description: An invalid amount produces Enter an amount between £1 and £500 while preserving entered choices

scenarios.label: Contribution failure
scenarios.description: Confirming the automation shows Contribution failed with working Try again and Pause automation actions

prototypeOnly: Balances, pots, and contribution dates are fixture data, not live accounts
Confirming automation records nothing; there is no ledger or transfer
Notifications, salary moments, and card-settings entry points are outside this prototype
Only the declarative runtime's screens, validation, and bindings are interactive
